alerts.title: Alert rules
alerts.intro: What becomes an emergency, what is only a signal, and how long to wait. These are the organization’s rules; any product can change its own.
alerts.productIntro: By default this product follows the organization’s rules. Changes here apply to it only.

levelHint.emergency: Needs action now. Message to the channels and the red strip on every screen until resolved.
levelHint.signal: Out of normal. No message: highlighted in its area and in the daily summary.
levelHint.off: Neither tells nor highlights. The data is still recorded.

monitor_down.title: Site or API down
monitor_down.body: A site or /health monitor failed 3 checks in a row. If it comes back before the wait, nobody is told.
monitor_down.info: Octadash checks every minute. One failure can be the network; three in a row is the site. Then it waits the minutes you set and, if it is still down, tells the channels and opens the red strip. Use 0 for checkout or login, where every minute counts.

heartbeat_missed.title: Heartbeat missed
heartbeat_missed.body: A cron job, backup or worker did not check in within its interval plus grace.
heartbeat_missed.info: Each heartbeat has its own interval and grace. When both pass without a check-in, the job is late and this rule decides what happens.
heartbeat_missed.note: Grace is set on each heartbeat.

cert_expiring.title: Certificate expiring
cert_expiring.body: The HTTPS certificate of a monitor expires soon.
cert_expiring.info: Octadash reads the certificate on every check. Most certificates renew on their own about 30 days before they expire; if one is still old this close, the renewal failed.

error_spike.title: Error spike
error_spike.body: A product’s errors in the last 15 minutes reach a multiple of its normal for this time of day, with a minimum so a quiet product does not fire on 3 errors.
error_spike.info: Normal is the same hour on each of the last 7 days. Errors of ignored issues never count. It closes on its own when the last 15 minutes fall back under the rule. A product with no history fires on the minimum alone.

key_event_stopped.title: Key event stopped
key_event_stopped.body: An event you marked as key (a sign-up, a payment) stops arriving at an hour it usually comes.
key_event_stopped.info: Octadash waits for the time the expected number of events normally takes at this hour (the same hour of the last 7 days), and never less than the minimum silence. Quiet hours wait longer on their own, and an event too rare at this hour (under 5 a day) never fires. It closes when the next event arrives. Mark key events in Set up Product usage.

watcher.title: Outside watcher
watcher.intro: If the Octadash server goes down, no alert goes out and nobody is told. The outside watcher fixes that: Octadash sends a signal every minute to an outside service, and that service tells you when the signals stop.
watcher.howIntro: About two minutes, on the free plan of Healthchecks.io.
watcher.step2: Create a check with a 1 minute period and a 5 minute grace time.
watcher.step3: Copy the check's ping URL (it starts with https://hc-ping.com/) and paste it below.
watcher.step4: On Healthchecks.io, choose where it tells you: email, Telegram or another channel. Use one that does not depend on this server.

warning.failingBody: Octadash cannot call the watcher's URL. If this goes on, the watcher will report Octadash as down.

monitorForm.homeBody: If it does, every check wakes the database, once a minute, all day. On Neon and other serverless databases that keeps it billed all the time. Better: a /health endpoint that answers without the database. Add it below and check that instead, or check the home page every 5 minutes.

monitorForm.expectedHint: Every N minutes, every day at a time, or a cron expression.
monitorForm.graceHint: How late it can be before it counts as missed.
monitorForm.graceInfo: A job that usually takes 10 minutes can run late on a slow night. Grace is how long Octadash waits after the expected time before calling it missed. Too short and you get false alarms; too long and you hear late. 30 minutes fits most backups.
monitorForm.callTitle: Call this address when the job finishes
monitorForm.failHint: Add /fail at the end when the job fails, so you hear at once instead of after the grace.

how.title: How it works
how.every: Checks every minute from this Octadash server.
how.three: Three failures in a row open an emergency; the alert rule decides how long to wait before telling anyone (now {minutes} min).
how.extras: The certificate, the http to https redirect and the response time come with every check.
how.database: Checks never touch your database unless the page does. That is why /health exists.

why.title: Why heartbeats
why.body: A backup that stops running fails in silence: nothing is down, nothing errors, and you find out the day you need it. A heartbeat turns silence into an emergency.
why.good: Good for backups, cron jobs, queue workers, certificate renewals and nightly imports.

trafficSetup.step1Note: Under 2.5 KB. Follows client-side navigation (single-page apps). Visits from localhost are skipped.
trafficSetup.returningBody: Off: a visitor is counted once per day, nothing is stored in the browser. On: a random id stays in the browser, so you see who came back. Adds data-visitor="persistent" to the code.
trafficSetup.returningInfo: Off is the private default: no cookie, nothing stored, the same person on two days counts twice. On stores a random id in the browser (localStorage). It identifies no one by name, but privacy laws such as GDPR and LGPD may ask for your visitors' consent before storing it. You can turn it on for one source and leave the others off.
trafficSetup.localBody: For testing on your machine. Adds data-local.
trafficSetup.readOnly: Only owners and admins change these options.
trafficSetup.waitingBody: Waiting for the first page view. Open any page of the site in another tab; it shows here in seconds.
trafficSetup.arrived: Page views are arriving. The last one was {path}, {time}.
trafficSetup.wontUse: I won't use Traffic in this product
privateItems: No cookies and nothing stored in the browser.
The IP is used to find the country and then thrown away.
A visitor is a hash that changes every day.
Bots are recognized and counted apart.
trafficSetup.noSource: No source for Traffic yet. Add one to get its code.

productSettings.footer: Monitors are in <uptime>Uptime</uptime>. Channels, members and the organization's rules are in <settings>Settings</settings>.

generalPage.title: General
generalPage.intro: Name, areas and what happens to {name}.
generalPage.name: Name
generalPage.nameHint: Shows in the picker, alerts and the TV mode.
generalPage.addressHint: Changes when you rename; old links keep working.

areas.title: Areas
areas.info: An area is on when it has a source or a monitor. Not used hides it from this product's pages, cards and alerts. Data that still arrives for an area not used is not stored, only counted, so a forgotten SDK shows up here.
areas.discarded: {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} arrived since, the last {time}. They were not stored.
areas.soonBody: This area is not built yet.

rulesCard.title: Alert rules
rulesCard.changed: {name} uses the organization's rules, {count, plural, one {with # changed here} other {with # changed here}}.

rulesPage.title: Alert rules
rulesPage.intro: {name} follows the organization's rules. Change one here and it holds for this product only.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.body: Delete {name} with {sources, plural, =0 {no sources} one {# source} other {# sources}}, {monitors, plural, =0 {no monitors} one {# monitor} other {# monitors}} and all their data. Keys stop working at once. This cannot be undone; you will be asked to type the name.
danger.dialogBody: Every source, monitor, emergency and all data of {name} are deleted. Keys stop working at once.

sourcesPage.title: Sources
sourcesPage.intro: The parts of {name} that send data to Octadash, each with its own key.
sourcesPage.info: One part of the product that sends data: the site, the API, the mobile app. Each has its own key, so you see which part stopped sending and can swap one key without touching the others. You don't pick areas here: one source feeds every area its data belongs to. A page view goes to Traffic, any other event to Product usage.
sourcesPage.empty: No sources yet. Setting up an area such as Traffic adds one, or add it here.
sourcesPage.alsoBody: These don't use a key, so they are managed in their area.
sourcesPage.monitors: {count, plural, one {# monitor checks} other {# monitors check}} the product from outside
sourcesPage.addBody: A name and where it runs. It gets its own key; the areas fill in as data arrives.
sourcesPage.name: Name

source.keyBody: The key only sends data; it can't read anything. That is why it is fine inside a web page.
source.dsnInfo: For code that already uses a Sentry SDK: put this DSN in place of the Sentry one and errors come to Octadash, with nothing else to change. It carries the same key, so rotating the key changes the DSN too.
source.rotateBody: A new key is made now. The old one keeps working for the time you pick, so you can deploy the new key first and lose nothing.
source.leakTitle: If the key leaked, pick Now
source.leakBody: Anyone with the key can send fake data to this product. Apps still on the old key stop sending until you deploy the new one.
source.afterBody: The page shows both keys: the new one to copy, and the old one with when it stops and a "Stop now" button. The DSN changes with the key.
source.platformHint: Only changes the install code shown.
source.localNote: Visits from localhost are an option of the install code.
source.deleteBody: Data already received stays. From then on, data with this key is refused.

tv.title: TV mode
tv.stopped: This TV link was stopped. Ask a manager for a new one.
tv.missing: Nothing to show here. The group or product may have been renamed or removed.

strip.label: Emergencies

tv.allUp: {count, plural, one {The product is up} other {All # products are up}}
tv.online: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody online} one {# person online} other {# people online}}

tv.incomplete: Numbers are not updating right now
tv.checksLabel: Checks in the last 4 hours: {ups} up, {downs} down

tvDialog.title: TV mode
tvDialog.body: A full screen for a TV on the wall: who is down, who is on it, and the numbers you pick. It updates by itself.
tvDialog.showBody: All products, a saved group or one product. Emergencies of every product reach the strip at the top anyway.
tvDialog.numbersBody: Pick up to {count}. A product that is down shows how long it has been down instead.
tvDialog.perPageBody: The screen turns the page every 20 seconds. Products in trouble stay on every page.
tvDialog.soundBody: A short beep when a product goes down. The TV asks once for permission to play sound.
tvDialog.linkInfo: For a TV that is not signed in. Anyone with the link sees this screen, and nothing else. Making a new link stops the old one. Stop it if the link leaks.
tvDialog.linkOnce: Copy it now. It is shown only once.
tvDialog.linkNone: No link yet. Signed-in people can open TV mode without one.
tvDialog.linkManagers: Only managers can make or stop the link.
tvDialog.linkReady: The private link is ready to copy.

errorsArea.title: Errors
errorsArea.intro: Errors from every product, grouped into issues: the same error in the same place counts once, with how many people it hit.
errorsArea.introGroup: Errors from the products of {group}, grouped into issues: the same error in the same place counts once.
errorsArea.introOne: Errors from {product}, grouped into issues: the same error in the same place counts once, with how many people it hit.
errorsArea.sending: {count, plural, one {# product} other {# products}} · {sending} send errors
errorsArea.incomplete: Some numbers are missing: the event store did not answer. The list of issues is complete.

empty.unresolved: No unresolved issues. New errors show up here as they arrive.
empty.new: No issue began in this period.
empty.regressed: No issue came back after being resolved.
empty.mine: You are not on any issue. Open one and press "I'm on it" so the team knows.

errorsArea.bars: {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} in the last 24 hours
errorsArea.foot: Same error in the same place = one issue. A resolved one that happens again comes back as Regressed.

none.title: No errors yet
none.body: Errors arrive in two ways, and both work with the key of any source of the product:
none.script: The Octadash script, the same one Traffic uses, already reports errors from the browser. Add data-release to the tag to know which release each one started in.
none.sentry: Code that already uses a Sentry SDK (any language) sends here by changing its DSN. Set up Errors shows the DSN and the code for each platform.
none.all: Pick a product to set up:

ignore.title: Ignore until
ignore.body: Hides the issue from the list until a condition you pick. When it is met, the issue comes back as Regressed, so nothing stays hidden by accident.
ignore.info: Hides the issue from the list until a condition you pick: it happens 100 more times, hits 50 more people, 24 hours pass, or never. When the condition is met it comes back as Regressed, so nothing stays hidden forever by accident.

issue.resolvedIn: Resolved in the next release after {release}. An event from {release} does not reopen it; one from any other release does.
issue.resolved: Resolved. The next event reopens it as Regressed.
issue.ignored: Ignored. It comes back as Regressed when its condition is met.
issue.chartLabel: {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} in the last 30 days, one bar per day
issue.nextReleaseHint: "Resolve in next release" closes it now and reopens it only if it happens again in a later release.
issue.noFrames: The SDK sent no stack for this error.
issue.noEvent: The events of this issue are older than the retention.
issue.noBreadcrumbs: The SDK sent nothing about what happened before. Sentry SDKs and the Octadash Node package send it.

errorsSetup.title: Set up Errors
errorsSetup.intro: Browser and server errors, grouped, with how many people each one hit and since when. Any Sentry SDK works by changing only the DSN.
errorsSetup.sourcesHint: This product already has a source. Use it and the same key starts sending errors too, or add a new one below.

status.waiting: for Errors · waiting for the first error

errorsSetup.name: Name
errorsSetup.nameHint: So you recognize it later: Site, API, Worker.
errorsSetup.dsnInfo: The address a Sentry SDK sends to. It holds this source’s key, which is not a secret: browsers see it too. Each source has its own, so you can tell the site from the API.
errorsSetup.dsnHint: The code below already has it.
errorsSetup.noteSdk: This is the Sentry SDK: Octadash reads what it sends. Set the release to see which version an error started in. Tested so far: @sentry/node 9.
errorsSetup.noteScript: The Octadash script reports uncaught errors and rejected promises (up to 10 per page). Change data-release with each deploy. It skips localhost unless the tag has data-local.
errorsSetup.noteOther: Any Sentry SDK works with this DSN. Without an SDK, POST the same event JSON to /o/v1/errors with the key.
errorsSetup.step2Body: Sends one error from this browser with this source’s key, to check the address and the key before you deploy.
errorsSetup.testSent: Sent. It shows below in a few seconds.
errorsSetup.testFailed: This browser could not reach the ingest address. Check OCTADASH_INGEST_URL.
errorsSetup.waitingBody: Waiting for the first error. Send the test above or trigger one in your app; it shows here in seconds.
errorsSetup.arrived: Errors are arriving. The last one: {error} ({time}).
errorsSetup.wontUse: I won’t use Errors in this product
